questions.question: What is the term used for the process of water evaporation through plant leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Transpiration**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Transpiration** is the biological process by which water is lost in the form of **water vapor** from the aerial parts of plants, primarily through the **leaves**.

• This process occurs through specialized tiny pores called **stomata**, which are usually located on the underside of the leaves.

• **Respiration** is the metabolic process where organisms exchange gases (oxygen and carbon dioxide) and break down food to release **energy**.

• **Photosynthesis** is the process used by plants to convert **light energy** into chemical energy (food) using **carbon dioxide** and **water** in the presence of **chlorophyll**.

• **Fermentation** is an **anaerobic** (without oxygen) biochemical process that breaks down organic substances like sugar into simpler compounds such as alcohol or lactic acid.

**Additional Information__**

• Transpiration creates a **negative pressure** known as **transpirational pull**, which helps in the upward movement of water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the top of the plant through the **xylem**.

• It plays a vital role in **thermoregulation**, as the evaporation of water helps in cooling the plant body during hot weather.

• The rate of transpiration is affected by various factors including **light**, **temperature**, **humidity**, and **wind speed**. High humidity generally decreases the rate of transpiration.

• The opening and closing of the stomatal pores are regulated by **guard cells**, which respond to the water status of the plant.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to dimensional analysis?

options.text: An equation that is dimensionally consistent is always physically correct.
Dimensional analysis can verify both the magnitude and the physical validity of an equation.
Trigonometric and logarithmic functions are valid only when applied to quantities that are dimensionless.
Refractive index has dimensions because it involves the speed of light.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Trigonometric and logarithmic functions are valid only when applied to quantities that are dimensionless.**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Trigonometric, logarithmic, and exponential functions** are mathematical operations that must take **dimensionless arguments**. For example, in the expression sin(theta) , the angle theta must be dimensionless. Similarly, in log(x) or e^x , x must be a pure number.

• An equation that is **dimensionally consistent** is not necessarily **physically correct**. For instance, the equation s = ut + at² is dimensionally consistent (all terms have dimensions of length), but it is physically incorrect because the correct kinematic formula is s = ut + (1)/(2)at² .

• **Dimensional analysis** cannot verify the **magnitude** or **dimensionless constants** in an equation. It only checks if the units on both sides of the equation are compatible.

• The **Refractive Index** is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in a medium ( n = c/v ). Since it is a ratio of two similar physical quantities (speeds), it is a **dimensionless quantity**.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Principle of Homogeneity of Dimensions** states that the dimensions of all the terms in a physical expression must be the same.

• Other common **dimensionless quantities** include **strain**, **relative density**, **solid angle**, and **plane angle**.

• While dimensional analysis is a powerful tool for checking the consistency of equations and deriving relations, its main limitation is its inability to determine **proportionality constants** or handle **summation/difference** of terms that are not of the same dimension.
</ul

• Statement 3: Marginal utility declines with each additional unit consumed. This is the core definition of the law. questions.question: Consider the following two statements about types of economies:**Statement I:** In a centrally planned economy, the government takes all major decisions regarding production, exchange, and consumption of goods and services.**Statement II:** In a market economy, economic activities are restricted to physical marketplaces where buyers and sellers must interact face-to-face.**Which of the above statements is/are correct**?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement I is correct**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Statement I** is correct because in a **centrally planned economy**, also known as a **command economy**, the **government** or a **central authority** takes all major decisions regarding the **production**, **exchange**, and **consumption** of goods and services. The **state** owns the **means of production** and decides what to produce, how to produce, and for whom to produce, often prioritizing **social welfare** over individual **profit**.

• **Statement II** is incorrect because a **market economy** is not restricted to **physical marketplaces** or **face-to-face interactions**. In economic terms, a **market** is any **mechanism** or **arrangement** that brings **buyers and sellers** together to facilitate **exchange**. In the **21st century**, this includes **e-commerce platforms**, **digital stock exchanges**, and **global financial networks** where transactions occur **electronically** without any **physical contact**.

• In a **centrally planned economy**, the **allocation of resources** is determined by a **central plan** rather than the **price mechanism**. This system was historically prevalent in countries like the **Soviet Union** and is still observed in **North Korea**. **Hence, Statement I is correct.**

• In a **market economy**, economic activities are guided by the **invisible hand**, a term coined by **Adam Smith** in **1776**. Prices are determined by the forces of **supply and demand**, and the **private sector** plays the most significant role in **resource allocation**. **Hence, Statement II is incorrect.**

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Mixed Economy**: This is an **economic system** that combines elements of both **market** and **centrally planned** economies. In a **mixed economy**, both the **public sector** and the **private sector** coexist. **India** adopted a **mixed economic model** after **Independence** in **1947** to balance **economic growth** with **social justice**.

• **Laissez-faire**: This is a **French** term meaning **leave alone**. It describes an **economic environment** where **transactions** between **private parties** are free from **government intervention**, such as **regulations**, **subsidies**, or **tariffs**. It is the purest form of a **capitalist market economy**.

• **Price Mechanism**: This refers to the **system** where **price** acts as a **signal** for **producers** and **consumers**. In a **market economy**, if the **demand** for a product increases, its **price** rises, signaling **producers** to increase **production**.

• **Socialist Economy**: Often associated with **central planning**, this system emphasizes **collective ownership** and the **reduction of income inequality**. The **government** ensures that **essential goods** and **services** like **healthcare** and **education** are accessible to all **citizens**.

• **Capitalist Economy**: Characterized by **private ownership** of **capital goods** and **investments** determined by **private decision**. The **United States**, **United Kingdom**, and **Japan** are prominent **examples** of **market-driven capitalist economies**.

**Important Points__**

• **Economic Problems**: Every **economy**, regardless of its type, must solve three fundamental **economic problems**: **What to produce** (selection of goods), **How to produce** (choice of technology/labor vs. capital), and **For whom to produce** (distribution of income).

• **Global Trends**: Since the **1991 LPG Reforms** (**Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization**), many **centrally planned economies** have transitioned toward **market-oriented** systems to improve **efficiency** and **global competitiveness**.

• **Role of Government**: Even in **market economies**, the **government** often intervenes to provide **public goods** (like **national defense**), regulate **monopolies**, and address **market failures** such as **pollution** or **economic recessions**.

• **Consumer Sovereignty**: In a **market economy**, **consumers** are considered **sovereign** because their **preferences** and **spending patterns** determine what **producers** will manufacture. In contrast, in a **centrally planned economy**, **consumer choice** is often **restricted** by **government quotas**.
</ul

questions.question:
In the following questions, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R).**Select the correct option from the following:
Assertion (A):** The Chalcolithic people in India did not benefit much from the technological knowledge of the Indus Valley Civilization.**Reason (R):** Chalcolithic cultures were generally younger and more isolated than the Indus people.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, but R is the correct explanation of A**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Assertion (A)** states that the **Chalcolithic people** in **India** did not benefit much from the **technological knowledge** of the **Indus Valley Civilization (IVC)**. This is because the **Chalcolithic** cultures were primarily **rural** and continued to use **copper** and **stone** tools, failing to adopt the advanced **urbanization**, **burnt bricks**, **standardized weights**, or the **script** developed by the **Harappans**. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***

• **Reason (R)** explains that **Chalcolithic cultures** were generally **younger** and more **isolated** than the **Indus people**. Most **Chalcolithic** sites, such as those of the **Malwa**, **Jorwe**, and **Ahar** cultures, flourished between **2100 BC** and **700 BC**, largely post-dating the **Mature Harappan Phase** (**2600 BC - 1900 BC**). Geographically, they were located in the **Deccan** and **Central India**, far from the **Indus basin**. ***Hence, statement R is correct.***

• The **isolation** and the **chronological gap** meant there was very little interaction or **cultural exchange** between the sophisticated **Bronze Age** urbanites of the **Indus** and the **rural** village communities of the **Chalcolithic** period.

• Because of this **geographical distance** and the fact that many of these cultures emerged as the **IVC** was already in decline or had disappeared, the **technological knowledge** (like **tin-bronze** metallurgy) did not diffuse to them. ***Therefore, R is the correct explanation of A.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Chalcolithic Age**: Also known as the **Copper-Stone Age**, it marked the first use of **metal** (**Copper**) alongside **stone tools**. It was a **rural** culture where people lived in **thatched houses** made of **mud** and **wattle-and-daub**.

• **Major Cultures**:

• **Ahar Culture**: Located in the **Banas Valley**, **Rajasthan** (approx. **2100 BC - 1500 BC**). It is also known as **Tambavati** because of the abundance of **copper**.

• **Kayatha Culture**: Found in **Madhya Pradesh** on the banks of the **Choti Sarali** river (approx. **2000 BC - 1800 BC**).

• **Malwa Culture**: Spread across **Central India** and **Maharashtra**, known for its distinct **painted pottery** (approx. **1700 BC - 1200 BC**).

• **Jorwe Culture**: The most extensive **Chalcolithic** culture in the **Deccan**, with major sites like **Inamgaon** and **Daimabad** (approx. **1400 BC - 700 BC**).

• **Pottery**: The **Chalcolithic** people were the first to use **painted pottery**, specifically **Black and Red Ware**, which was wheel-turned and decorated with white linear designs.

• **Agriculture and Diet**: They practiced **subsistence agriculture**, growing **wheat**, **barley**, **rice**, and **lentils**. They also domesticated **cows**, **sheep**, **goats**, and **pigs**, but were not acquainted with the **horse**.

**Important Points__**

• **Metallurgy Difference**: While the **Indus Valley Civilization** mastered the production of **Bronze** (an alloy of **copper** and **tin**), the **Chalcolithic** people mostly used **unalloyed copper**. This limited the strength and utility of their tools compared to the **Harappans**.

• **Burial Customs**: In the **Jorwe culture** of **Maharashtra**, the dead were buried in **urns** placed under the floor of the house in a **North-to-South** direction, accompanied by **grave goods** like **pottery** and **copper** objects.

• **Religious Beliefs**: Evidence of **Mother Goddess** figurines and **Bull** worship (terracotta bulls) suggests a **fertility cult** similar to other ancient agrarian societies.

• **Copper Hoards**: Distinct from the **Harappan** tools, various **copper hoards** containing **celts**, **harpoons**, and **anthropomorphs** have been found in the **Ganga-Yamuna Doab**, belonging to the **Ochre Coloured Pottery (OCP)** culture phase.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following powers did Jammu and Kashmir have under Article 370?

options.text: Decision-making in all matters except defence, foreign affairs, and communications

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of the above**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Article 370** of the **Indian Constitution** provided a special autonomous status to the state of **Jammu and Kashmir**. This article allowed the state to have **its own Constitution**, which was separate from the Constitution of India. This document governed the internal administration and legal framework of the state. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

• Under the provisions of **Article 370**, the state was permitted to fly its own **separate flag** alongside the **National Flag of India**. The state flag was **red** in color with **three white vertical stripes** representing the three regions of the state (Jammu, Kashmir, and Ladakh) and a **white plough**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***

• The **Parliament of India** had limited legislative powers over the state. Its authority was restricted primarily to matters of **defence, foreign affairs, finance, and communications**. For the application of any other central laws, the **concurrence of the State Government** was mandatory, giving the state significant **decision-making power** in most internal matters. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

• Because all the mentioned powers—having a separate constitution, a distinct flag, and restricted central legislative jurisdiction—were integral features of the special status granted by **Article 370**, the correct choice is **All of the above**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Historical Context:** **Article 370** was incorporated into the **Constitution of India** on **October 17, 1949**, as a **temporary provision**. It was drafted by **N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar** to manage the unique transition of the state into the **Union of India** following the **Instrument of Accession** signed by **Maharaja Hari Singh** in **1947**.

• **Article 35A:** This was a significant provision derived from **Article 370**, introduced through a **Presidential Order in 1954**. It empowered the **Jammu and Kashmir State Legislature** to define **permanent residents** of the state and provide them with exclusive rights regarding **government jobs**, **scholarships**, and the **purchase of immovable property**.

• **Abrogation of Article 370:** On **August 5, 2019**, the **President of India** issued the **Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order, 2019**, which effectively revoked the special status. This action made the **Constitution of India** fully applicable to the region and ended the state's separate constitution and flag.

• **Reorganization:** Following the abrogation, the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019** was enacted. This led to the **bifurcation** of the state into two **Union Territories**: **Jammu and Kashmir** (with a legislative assembly) and **Ladakh** (without a legislative assembly), effective from **October 31, 2019**.

**Important Points__**

• **Legislative Impact:** Before **2019**, **Article 360** (Financial Emergency) of the Indian Constitution did not apply to **Jammu and Kashmir**. Furthermore, the **Directive Principles of State Policy** and various **Fundamental Rights** were applicable only in a modified form or through state-specific legislation.

• **Judicial Oversight:** While the **Supreme Court of India** had jurisdiction over the state, the **High Court of Jammu and Kashmir** held a unique position, and certain central laws like the **Right to Information (RTI) Act** or the **Right to Education (RTE) Act** were not automatically applicable until the state legislature passed corresponding laws.

• **Current Status:** Since **October 2019**, the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** has replaced the **Ranbir Penal Code (RPC)**, and all **central laws** and **welfare schemes** are now directly implemented in the **Union Territories** of **Jammu and Kashmir** and **Ladakh**.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Akshaya Patra Foundation** is a **not-for-profit organization** based in **Bengaluru**, India, that operates on a **Public-Private Partnership (PPP)** model with the **Government of India** and various **State Governments**.

• It is the primary organization that supports the **distribution of meals** under the **PM POSHAN** (formerly **Mid-Day Meal**) scheme in several states across India, serving millions of children every day to eliminate classroom hunger.

• The foundation was established in the year **2000** and started by serving **1,500 children** in **5 schools**; today, it has scaled up to reach over **2 million children** across multiple states and union territories.

• **UNICEF** (United Nations Children's Fund) and **WHO** (World Health Organization) are international bodies that provide **technical expertise**, **policy guidelines**, and **funding for health initiatives**, but they do not typically manage the daily logistics of meal distribution in Indian schools. ***Hence, options 1 and 3 are incorrect.***

• **NITI Aayog** is the premier **policy think tank** of the **Government of India**, providing directional and policy inputs; it monitors and evaluates the performance of the **PM POSHAN** scheme but does not act as an implementing agency for food distribution. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

• The **Akshaya Patra Foundation** utilizes **centralized kitchens** in urban areas, which are highly automated facilities capable of preparing up to **100,000 meals** in a few hours, ensuring high standards of **hygiene** and **nutrition**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Akshaya Patra Foundation.***

__

• The scheme was renamed from the **National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education** (Mid-Day Meal Scheme) in **September 2021** and has been extended to include children in **Balvatikas** (pre-primary classes).

• The **Ministry of Education** is the nodal ministry responsible for the implementation of this scheme at the national level, covering approximately **11.80 crore children** in **11.20 lakh schools**.

• The nutritional norms for the **Primary level** (Classes 1-5) are **450 calories** and **12 grams of protein**, while for the **Upper Primary level** (Classes 6-8), the norms are **700 calories** and **20 grams of protein**.

• The scheme aims to address two major issues: **malnutrition** among children and the **socio-economic gap** in education by incentivizing parents to send their children to school.

**Important Points__**

• **Historical Context**: **Tamil Nadu** was the first state in **India** to introduce the **Mid-Day Meal Scheme** in the **1960s** under the leadership of Chief Minister **K. Kamaraj**.

• **Legal Mandate**: In **November 2001**, the **Supreme Court of India** passed a landmark judgment in the **PUCL vs Union of India** case, making it mandatory for all **State Governments** to provide cooked mid-day meals.

• **Funding Pattern**: The cost of the scheme is shared between the **Centre** and the **States** in a **60:40** ratio for general category states, **90:10** for **North-Eastern** and **Himalayan States**, and **100%** for **Union Territories** without a legislature.

questions.question: Which harvest festival is celebrated in Punjab during January?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lohri**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Lohri** is a popular **harvest festival** celebrated primarily in the **Punjab** region of the Indian subcontinent. It is observed with great enthusiasm by both **Sikhs** and **Hindus** to mark the end of the peak winter season.

• The festival is celebrated every year on the **13th of January**, just a day before **Makar Sankranti**. It signifies the sun's entry into the northern hemisphere, known as **Uttarayana**, leading to longer days and shorter nights.

• It is traditionally associated with the harvest of **Rabi crops**, particularly **sugarcane**. Farmers in **Punjab** and **Haryana** offer prayers and thanks to the **Almighty** for a successful harvest and pray for prosperity in the coming season.

• The central ritual of **Lohri** is the lighting of a **bonfire** after sunset. People gather around the fire, sing traditional folk songs, and perform **Bhangra** and **Gidda**. Offerings of **til** (sesame seeds), **gajak**, **gur** (jaggery), **popcorn**, and **rewri** are thrown into the fire as a tribute to the **God of Fire (Agni)**.

• The festival is also deeply linked to the legend of **Dulla Bhatti**, a local hero who lived during the reign of **Emperor Akbar**. He is remembered for rescuing young girls from being sold into slavery and arranging their marriages. The famous folk song **Sunder Mundriye** is sung during the celebrations to honor his bravery.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Pongal**: This is a **four-day** harvest festival celebrated in the state of **Tamil Nadu**. It usually falls between **January 14th and 17th**. It is dedicated to the **Sun God (Surya)** and involves the ritual of boiling fresh rice in milk in a clay pot until it overflows, symbolizing abundance.

• **Bihu**: Specifically **Magh Bihu** (also known as **Bhogali Bihu**), is the harvest festival of **Assam** celebrated in **January**. It marks the end of the harvesting season in the month of **Maagha**. People build temporary huts called **Meji** and **Bhelaghar** from bamboo and thatch, which are burned the next morning.

• **Makar Sankranti**: This is a major pan-Indian festival that marks the transition of the **Sun** into the zodiac sign of **Capricorn (Makara)**. While it is celebrated on **January 14th or 15th**, it is known by various names such as **Uttarayan** in **Gujarat** (famous for kite flying), **Poush Sankranti** in **West Bengal**, and **Khichdi** in **Uttar Pradesh**.

• **Vaisakhi**: Although it is also a harvest festival in **Punjab**, it is celebrated in the month of **April** (usually **April 13th or 14th**). It marks the ripening of the **wheat (Rabi) crop** and also commemorates the formation of the **Khalsa Panth** by **Guru Gobind Singh** in **1699**.

**Important Points__**

• **Social Significance**: **Lohri** holds special importance for families that have recently celebrated a **wedding** or the **birth of a child**. The 'first Lohri' of a new bride or a newborn is celebrated with extra fervor and grand feasts.

• **Traditional Cuisine**: The traditional dinner served during **Lohri** consists of **Sarson da Saag** (mustard greens) and **Makki di Roti** (cornbread), which are seasonal staples in **North India**.

• **Geographical Reach**: While it is the primary festival of **Punjab**, it is also widely celebrated in **Delhi**, **Himachal Pradesh**, and **Jammu** due to the significant **Punjabi** diaspora and cultural influence in these regions.

• **Environmental Aspect**: In recent years, there has been a growing awareness to celebrate **Eco-friendly Lohri** by reducing the size of bonfires to prevent excessive air pollution, while still maintaining the cultural essence of the festival.
</ul

• The central characters include **Juggut Singh**, a local dacoit who ultimately sacrifices himself to save a train carrying **Muslim** refugees to **Pakistan**, and **Iqbal Singh**, an educated social reformer who finds himself helpless against the rising tide of communal frenzy.

• The book is acclaimed for its **humanistic perspective**, as it avoids taking political sides and instead focuses on the shared suffering, moral dilemmas, and the loss of humanity during the **Partition**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Khushwant Singh (1915–2014):** He was a prominent **Indian author**, **lawyer**, and **journalist**. He served as the editor of **The Illustrated Weekly of India** and was a member of the **Rajya Sabha**. He was awarded the **Padma Bhushan** in **1974** and the **Padma Vibhushan** in **2007**.

questions.question: Which architectural style is the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Tamil Nadu known for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dravidian**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Brihadeeswarar Temple**, located in **Thanjavur**, **Tamil Nadu**, is one of the most celebrated examples of **Dravidian Architecture**. This style is characterized by its pyramid-shaped towers, known as **Vimanas**, and large temple complexes. **Dravidian** architecture is the correct answer because the temple exhibits all the classic features of this South Indian style, such as the **Vimana**, **Mandapa**, and **Gopurams**.

• The temple was built by the **Chola Emperor Raja Raja Chola I** between **1003 AD** and **1010 AD**. It was a symbol of the **Chola Dynasty's** power and their devotion to **Lord Shiva**.

• A unique feature of this temple is its **Vimana** (the tower over the sanctum), which stands at a height of **216 feet** (approximately **66 meters**). At the time of its construction, it was one of the tallest structures in the world.

• The temple is constructed entirely out of **granite**. This is a remarkable feat because there are no granite sources within a **60-kilometer** radius of **Thanjavur**, implying a massive logistical effort during the **11th century**.

• The temple is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage Site** known as the **Great Living Chola Temples**, which also includes the **Brihadisvara Temple** at **Gangaikonda Cholapuram** and the **Airavatesvara Temple** at **Darasuram**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Nagara Style**: This architectural style is predominant in **Northern India**. Unlike the **Dravidian** style, the **Nagara** style features a beehive-shaped tower called a **Shikhara**. It typically does not have the massive **Gopurams** (gateways) or the large water tanks that are common in South Indian temples. Examples include the **Kandariya Mahadeva Temple** in **Khajuraho** and the **Sun Temple** in **Konark**.

• **Vesara Style**: This is a hybrid style that combines elements of both **Nagara** and **Dravidian** architecture. It flourished in the **Deccan** region of India, particularly under the **Chalukya** and **Hoysala** dynasties. The **Chennakesava Temple** at **Belur** is a famous example of this style.

• **Indo-Saracenic Style**: This is a **revivalist** architectural style used by **British architects** in India during the late **19th century**. It blends **Indo-Islamic**, **Hindu**, and **Gothic** elements. Notable examples include the **Victoria Memorial** in **Kolkata** and the **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus** in **Mumbai**.

• **Chola Art and Culture**: The **Chola** period is known as the **Golden Age** of **Tamil** culture. Apart from architecture, the **Cholas** were famous for their **bronze sculptures**, particularly the **Nataraja** (the dancing Shiva), and their extensive maritime trade across **Southeast Asia**.

**Important Points__**

• The **Kumbam** (the apex or the bulbous structure at the top of the tower) of the **Brihadeeswarar Temple** is carved out of a **single rock** and is estimated to weigh about **80 tons**.

• The temple is also known as **Dakshina Meru** (the Meru of the South). The **Shiva Linga** inside the sanctum is one of the largest in India, standing **3.7 meters** tall.

questions.question: In which year did the Indian Constitution come into effect?

__
 
• The **Constitution of India** officially came into effect on **January 26, 1950**. This date was specifically chosen to commemorate the declaration of **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence) by the **Indian National Congress** in **1930**.
 
• While the Constitution was **adopted** by the **Constituent Assembly** on **November 26, 1949**, it was legally enforced two months later to mark the historical significance of **Republic Day**. ***Hence, the option 1950 is correct.***
 
• With the enforcement of the Constitution, the **Government of India Act 1935** was repealed, and India transitioned from a **British Dominion** to a **Sovereign Democratic Republic**.
 
• The **Constituent Assembly** took precisely **2 years, 11 months, and 18 days** to complete the drafting of the world's lengthiest written constitution.
 
• At the time of its commencement in **1950**, the Constitution consisted of a **Preamble**, **395 Articles** (divided into **22 Parts**), and **8 Schedules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of other years mentioned in the options:**
 
 
• **1947:** This year marks the **Indian Independence Act**, through which India gained freedom from British rule on **August 15, 1947**. However, the country continued to be governed by modified colonial laws until the Constitution was enacted.
 
• **1949:** On **November 26, 1949**, the drafting process was finalized, and the document was signed by the members of the **Constituent Assembly**. This day is now celebrated annually as **Constitution Day** (Samvidhan Divas).
 
• **1952:** This year is significant as it saw the conclusion of India's **first General Elections** (held between October 1951 and February 1952) and the formation of the first democratically elected **Parliament** of India.
 
 
 
• **The Drafting Committee:**
 
 
• The **Drafting Committee**, which was responsible for preparing the final text, was chaired by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, who is recognized as the **Father of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• Other prominent members included **Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer**, **N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar**, and **K.M. Munshi**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Original Manuscript:** The original Constitution of India was not printed but **handwritten** (calligraphed) in both **Hindi and English** by **Prem Behari Narain Raizada**.
 
• **Artistic Decoration:** Each page of the original document was uniquely decorated by artists from **Shantiniketan**, including **Nandalal Bose** and **Beohar Rammanohar Sinha**.
 
• **Universal Adult Franchise:** One of the most revolutionary features of the 1950 Constitution was the introduction of **Universal Adult Suffrage**, granting every citizen above a certain age (originally **21 years**, later reduced to **18 years** by the **61st Amendment**) the right to vote regardless of gender, caste, or education.
 
• **Borrowed Features:** The Indian Constitution is often described as a "bag of borrowings" because it incorporated best practices from various countries, such as **Parliamentary Democracy** from the **UK**, **Fundamental Rights** from the **USA**, and **Directive Principles** from **Ireland**.

questions.question: Which of the following statement about federalism in India is true?

options.text: States have the right to secede from the Union
There is rigid division of powers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Union has overriding authority**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 1** of the **Constitution of India** describes India as a **"Union of States"** rather than a "Federation of States." This terminology signifies that the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among the states, and consequently, no state has the **right to secede** from the Union. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• The Indian **federal system** follows a **flexible division of powers** rather than a rigid one. While the **Seventh Schedule** provides three lists (Union, State, and Concurrent), the Union government holds **residuary powers** and can influence state legislation under specific conditions. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• The **Union has overriding authority** over the states, which is a defining feature of India's **quasi-federal** structure. Under **Article 249**, Parliament can legislate on subjects in the State List in the **national interest** if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution. Similarly, during a **National Emergency (Article 352)**, the federal structure transforms into a unitary one. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• In India, states are not **sovereign entities**. The **Parliament of India** has the power under **Article 3** to increase or diminish the area of any state, alter its boundaries, or change its name, even without the state legislature's ultimate consent. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• The **supremacy of the Union** is also evident in the **Concurrent List**, where in case of a conflict between a central law and a state law, the **central law prevails** as per **Article 254**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Indian Federalism:** 
 
 
• Experts like **K.C. Wheare** have described the Indian Constitution as **"quasi-federal"** because it contains both federal and unitary features with a strong tilt towards the **Center**.
 
• Other scholars, such as **Morris Jones**, termed it **"bargaining federalism,"** while **Granville Austin** called it **"cooperative federalism"** because of the interdependence between the Union and the States.
 
 
 
• **The Seventh Schedule:** 
 
 
• The **Union List** contains **100 subjects** (originally 97) such as **defense, foreign affairs, and banking**, over which only the Parliament can legislate.
 
• The **State List** consists of **61 subjects** (originally 66) like **police, public health, and agriculture**.
 
• The **Concurrent List** includes **52 subjects** (originally 47) such as **education, forests, and marriage**, where both tiers can legislate.
 
 
 
• **Unitary Features:** Features like a **Single Constitution**, **Single Citizenship**, **Integrated Judiciary**, and the appointment of the **Governor** by the **President** strengthen the Union's position.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **S.R. Bommai vs Union of India (1994):** In this landmark judgment, the **Supreme Court** ruled that **federalism** is a part of the **"Basic Structure"** of the Constitution. However, it also acknowledged the **superior powers** of the Union in matters of national integrity and security.
 
• **Residuary Powers:** Under **Article 248**, the power to legislate on any matter not mentioned in any of the three lists (Residuary Powers) is vested solely in the **Union Parliament**. This is a departure from the **U.S. federal model** where residuary powers rest with the states.
 
• **Article 356 (President's Rule):** This provision allows the Union to take over the **executive and legislative powers** of a state if the constitutional machinery fails, further illustrating the **overriding authority** of the Union.
</ul

questions.question: The lengths of the diagonals of a rhombus compare as 3 times some value to 4 times that same value. If the area of the rhombus is 216 cm², what are the actual lengths of the two diagonals?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of diagonals d₁ : d₂ = 3 : 4

Area = 1/2 × (Product of ratio parts) × x²

216 = 1/2 × 3 × 4 × x² ⇒ 216 = 6x²

x² = 36 ⇒ x = 6

Actual diagonals = 3 × 6 and 4 × 6 = 18 cm and 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm and 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of diagonals = 3 : 4, Area of rhombus = 216 cm².

**Formula Used:** Area of Rhombus = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d4185ae34bb1acf87843d553473cb5a4cf84a4b323fe6fbc295b60d0f3dd864.png] 

⇒ Let the lengths of the diagonals be 3x and 4x.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 3x × 4x

⇒ 216 = 6x²

⇒ x² = 216 ÷ 6

⇒ x² = 36

⇒ x = √36 = 6

⇒ First diagonal (d₁) = 3 × 6 = 18 cm

⇒ Second diagonal (d₂) = 4 × 6 = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm and 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rhombus

A rhombus is a quadrilateral with all four sides equal. Opposite angles are equal and adjacent angles are supplementary (sum to 180°).

Diagonal Property

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles (90°).

Side-Diagonal Relation

If side is 'a' and diagonals are d₁ and d₂, then 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

Perimeter of Rhombus

The perimeter is calculated as 4 × side.</p

⇒ √121 = 11

BODMAS Rule

Operations inside **brackets** must be completed before performing multiplication outside the brackets.

Algebraic Identity for Multiplication

questions.question: Let a = 2⁴ · 3² · 5 and b = 2² · 3 · 7³. which of the following is true?

options.text: L.C.M(a, b) × GCD(a, b) = a + b

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**LCM** is the product of the **highest powers** of all prime factors present in the numbers.

Highest powers: 2 → 2⁴, 3 → 3², 5 → 5¹, 7 → 7³.

**LCM(a, b)** = 2⁴ × 3² × 5 × 7³.

**GCD** is the product of the **lowest powers** of common prime factors: 2² × 3.

Comparing with options, only the first statement matches the calculated **LCM**.

**∴ The correct answer is L.C.M(a, b) = 2⁴ × 3² × 5 × 7³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a = 2⁴ × 3² × 5

b = 2² × 3 × 7³

**Formula Used:**

**LCM (Least Common Multiple)** = Product of the highest power of each prime factor involved in the numbers.

**GCD (Greatest Common Divisor)** = Product of the lowest power of each common prime factor.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factors involved in both numbers are **2, 3, 5, and 7**.

⇒ For **LCM**, we take the maximum exponent for each prime:

⇒ Max power of 2 = 2⁴

⇒ Max power of 3 = 3²

⇒ Max power of 5 = 5¹

⇒ Max power of 7 = 7³

⇒ **LCM(a, b)** = 2⁴ × 3² × 5 × 7³

⇒ For **GCD**, we take the minimum exponent for each common prime:

⇒ Min power of 2 = 2²

⇒ Min power of 3 = 3¹

⇒ **GCD(a, b)** = 2² × 3 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is L.C.M(a, b) = 2⁴ × 3² × 5 × 7³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between LCM and GCD

For any two positive integers x and y, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **LCM** and **GCD**: x × y = LCM(x, y) × GCD(x, y).

GCD of Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers have no common prime factors, their **GCD** is 1, and they are called **co-prime** or relatively prime numbers.

Prime Factorization Method

This method expresses each number as a product of **prime powers**, making it easy to identify the highest and lowest powers for **LCM** and **GCD** respectively.

questions.question: An online seller purchases a laptop at ₹40,000. He lists it at a 25% markup. Due to a festive sale, he gives a flat 10% discount on the listed price and offers free shipping costing him ₹500. What is the net profit or loss percentage?

Effective Selling Price factor = 1.25 (Markup) × 0.90 (Discount) = 1.125

Selling Price (SP) = 40,000 × 1.125 = ₹45,000

Total effective Cost Price (CP) = 40,000 + 500 (Shipping) = ₹40,500

Net Profit % = [(45,000 − 40,500) ÷ 40,500] × 100 = (4,500 ÷ 40,500) × 100 = 1/9 × 100 = 11.11%

**∴ The correct answer is 11.11%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ SP = 50,000 − (0.10 × 50,000) = 50,000 − 5,000 = ₹45,000

⇒ Total effective cost for seller = Purchase Price + Shipping

⇒ Total CP = 40,000 + 500 = ₹40,500

⇒ Net Profit = SP − Total CP = 45,000 − 40,500 = ₹4,500

⇒ Net Profit % = (Net Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

⇒ Net Profit % = (4,500 ÷ 40,500) × 100 = 1/9 × 100 = 11.11%

**∴ The correct answer is 11.11%.**

questions.question: If sec theta + tan theta = p , what is the value of sec theta in terms of p?

Using the identity sec² θ − tan² θ = 1.

If sec θ + tan θ = p, then sec θ − tan θ = 1/p.

Adding both equations: (sec θ + tan θ) + (sec θ − tan θ) = p + 1/p.

2 sec θ = (p² + 1)/p ⇒ sec θ = (p² + 1)/2p.

**∴ The correct answer is (p² + 1)/2p.**

**Given:** sec θ + tan θ = p --- (i)

**Formula Used:** sec² θ − tan² θ = 1

⇒ sec θ − tan θ = 1/p --- (ii)

⇒ Adding equation (i) and (ii):

⇒ (sec θ + tan θ) + (sec θ − tan θ) = p + 1/p

⇒ 2 sec θ = (p² + 1)/p

⇒ sec θ = (p² + 1)/2p

**∴ The correct answer is (p² + 1)/2p.**

For any value p, the expressions (p² − 1), 2p, and (p² + 1) always form a Pythagorean triplet.</p

questions.question: Consider two points on the ground, at distances a and b from the base of a tower (a > b) from the foot of the tower and in the same straight line with it are 30° and 60° respectively. The height of the tower is:

If the angles of elevation from two points at distances **a** and **b** from the base are **complementary** (sum = 90°), the height **h** is always the **geometric mean** of the distances.

Given angles: 30° and 60° ⇒ Sum = 30° + 60° = 90°.

Since the angles are complementary, **h = √(a × b)**.

**∴ The correct answer is √ab.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Let the height of the tower be **h**.

⇒ tan 30° = h / a

⇒ **h = a / √3** --- (Equation 1)

⇒ In the smaller triangle (distance b):

⇒ tan 60° = h / b

⇒ √3 = h / b

⇒ **h = b × √3** --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Multiplying Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ h × h = (a / √3) × (b × √3)

⇒ **h = √ab**

questions.question: Converting the decimal number 241 to the binary number system we get:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify powers of 2 less than or equal to 241: 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1.

Subtract the largest power of 2 from the number: 241 − 128 = 113; 113 − 64 = 49; 49 − 32 = 17; 17 − 16 = 1; 1 − 1 = 0.

Assign '1' to used weights (128, 64, 32, 16, 1) and '0' to unused weights (8, 4, 2).

Binary representation: 1(128) 1(64) 1(32) 1(16) 0(8) 0(4) 0(2) 1(1) → 11110001.

**∴ The correct answer is 11110001.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Decimal Number = 241

Formula Used: Successive division by 2 (Base of Binary System).

⇒ 241 ÷ 2 = 120, Remainder = 1

⇒ 120 ÷ 2 = 60, Remainder = 0

⇒ 60 ÷ 2 = 30, Remainder = 0

⇒ 30 ÷ 2 = 15, Remainder = 0

⇒ 15 ÷ 2 = 7, Remainder = 1

⇒ 7 ÷ 2 = 3, Remainder = 1

⇒ 3 ÷ 2 = 1, Remainder = 1

⇒ 1 ÷ 2 = 0, Remainder = 1

Note: The binary number is formed by reading remainders from the last division (MSB) to the first (LSB).

⇒ Binary = 11110001

**∴ The correct answer is 11110001.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Binary Number System

It is a base-2 system that uses only two digits (0 and 1). Every digit's position corresponds to a power of 2, e.g., 2ⁿ.

MSB and LSB

MSB (Most Significant Bit) is the leftmost bit having the highest weight, while LSB (Least Significant Bit) is the rightmost bit with a weight of 2⁰.

Hexadecimal Conversion

Binary numbers can be converted to Hexadecimal (Base-16) by grouping bits into sets of four from the right. Here, 1111 0001 → F1₁₆.</p

questions.question: Which of the following relationship between the sets of integers, rational numbers, and real numbers holds good?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Numbers follow a hierarchical inclusion: Natural ⊆ Whole ⊆ Integers ⊆ Rationals ⊆ Reals.

Every Integer (Z) can be expressed as a fraction Z/1, so Z is a subset of Rational numbers (Q).

The set of Real numbers (R) includes all Rational (Q) and Irrational numbers.

Thus, the nested relationship is Z ⊆ Q ⊆ R.

**∴ The correct answer is Z ⊆ Q ⊆ R.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sets Z (Integers), Q (Rational Numbers), and R (Real Numbers).

**Property:** A ⊆ B means every element of set A is contained within set B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b608a81024f893ba20589f8e55e90ea098d69db9a86a2c505cbb4757298d9f8.png] 

⇒ Integers (Z) = {..., −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, ...}

⇒ Rational Numbers (Q) = {p/q : p, q ∈ Z, q ≠ 0}

⇒ Since any integer n = n/1, every integer is a rational number ∴ Z ⊆ Q.

⇒ Real Numbers (R) consist of all points on the number line (Rational ∪ Irrational).

⇒ Since all rational numbers are part of the real number line ∴ Q ⊆ R.

⇒ Combining these: Z ⊆ Q ⊆ R.

**∴ The correct answer is Z ⊆ Q ⊆ R.**

**__Additional Information__**

Natural Numbers (N)

The set {1, 2, 3, ...} is the most basic subset of integers, denoted as N ⊆ Z.

Irrational Numbers (I)

Numbers like √2, π, and e that cannot be written as p/q. Note that Q ∩ I = ∅ and Q ∪ I = R.

Complex Numbers (C)

The set of numbers in the form a + bi, where a and b are real numbers and i = √−1. R is a subset of C (R ⊆ C).</p
